text: Mr. Trump, I want to ask you about one last question in this topic. You have been warning at rallies recently that this election is rigged and that Hillary Clinton is in the process of trying to steal it from you.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I will look at it at the time. I’m not looking at anything now. I’ll look at it at the time.

speaker: Moderator
text: But, sir, there’s…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: If you look—excuse me, Chris—if you look at your voter rolls, you will see millions of people that are registered to vote—millions, this isn’t coming from me—this is coming from Pew Report and other places—millions of people that are registered to vote that shouldn’t be registered to vote.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Chris, she should never have been allowed to run for the presidency based on what she did with e-mails and so many other things.

speaker: Moderator
text: But, sir, there is a tradition in this country—in fact, one of the prides of this country—is the peaceful transition of power and that no matter how hard-fought a campaign is, that at the end of the campaign that the loser concedes to the winner. Not saying that you’re necessarily going to be the loser or the winner, but that the loser concedes to the winner and that the country comes together in part for the good of the country. Are you saying you’re not prepared now to commit to that principle?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: What I’m saying is that I will tell you at the time. I’ll keep you in suspense. OK?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, Chris, let me respond to that, because that’s horrifying. You know, every time Donald thinks things are not going in his direction, he claims whatever it is, is rigged against him.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Should have gotten it. [laughter]

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: This is—this is a mindset. This is how Donald thinks. And it’s funny, but it’s also really troubling.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: So that is not the way our democracy works. We’ve been around for 240 years. We’ve had free and fair elections. We’ve accepted the outcomes when we may not have liked them. And that is what must be expected of anyone standing on a debate stage during a general election. You know, President Obama said the other day when you’re whining before the game is even finished… [applause]

speaker: Moderator
text: Hold on. Hold on, folks. Hold on, folks.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … it just shows you’re not up to doing the job. And let’s—you know, let’s be clear about what he is saying and what that means. He is denigrating—he’s talking down our democracy. And I, for one, am appalled that somebody who is the nominee of one of our two major parties would take that kind of position.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think what the FBI did and what the Department of Justice did, including meeting with her husband, the attorney general, in the back of an airplane on the tarmac in Arizona, I think it’s disgraceful. I think it’s a disgrace.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think we’ve never had a situation so bad in this country. [applause]

speaker: Moderator
text: Hold on, folks. This doesn’t do any good for anyone. Let’s please continue the debate, and let’s move on to the subject of foreign hot spots.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I am encouraged that there is an effort led by the Iraqi army, supported by Kurdish forces, and also given the help and advice from the number of special forces and other Americans on the ground. But I will not support putting American soldiers into Iraq as an occupying force. I don’t think that is in our interest, and I don’t think that would be smart to do. In fact, Chris, I think that would be a big red flag waving for ISIS to reconstitute itself.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, same question. If we are able to push ISIS out of Mosul and out of Iraq, will—would you be willing to put U.S. troops in there to prevent their return or something else?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Let me tell you, Mosul is so sad. We had Mosul. But when she left, when she took everybody out, we lost Mosul. Now we’re fighting again to get Mosul. The problem with Mosul and what they wanted to do is they wanted to get the leaders of ISIS who they felt were in Mosul.

speaker: Moderator
text: Sir, your two minutes are up.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: The point is, the big winner is going to be Iran.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, you know, once again, Donald is implying that he didn’t support the invasion of Iraq. I said it was a mistake. I’ve said that years ago. He has consistently denied what is…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … a very clear fact that…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … before the invasion, he supported it. And, you know, I just want everybody to go Google it. Google “Donald Trump Iraq.” And you will see the dozens of sources which verify that he was for the invasion of Iraq.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And you can actually hear the audio of him saying that. Now, why does that matter? Well, it matters because he has not told the truth about that position. I guess he believes it makes him look better now to contrast with me because I did vote for it.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Chris, we don’t gain anything.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: He has all the conspiracy theories…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Iran is taking over Iraq.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, it’s…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Iran is taking over Iraq. We don’t gain anything.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: This conspiracy theory, which he’s been spewing out for quite some time.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We would’ve gained if they did it by surprise…[crosstalk]

speaker: Moderator
text: Wait, wait, wait, Secretary Clinton, it’s an open discussion.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: He says…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We would have gained if they did it by surprise.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary, please let Mr. Trump speak.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … unfit, and he proves it every time he talks.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, you are the one that’s unfit. You know, WikiLeaks just actually came out—John Podesta said some horrible things about you, and, boy, was he right. He said some beauties. And you know, Bernie Sanders, he said you have bad judgment. You do.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, you should ask Bernie Sanders who he’s supporting for president. And he has said…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Which is a big mistake.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … as he has campaigned for me around the country, you are the most dangerous person to run for president in the modern history of America. I think he’s right.

speaker: Moderator
text: Let’s turn to Aleppo. Mr. Trump, in the last debate, you were both asked about the situation in the Syrian city of Aleppo. speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s a catastrophe. I mean…

text: It’s a catastrophe, but there…

text: … it’s a mess.

text: There are a quarter of…

text: Have you seen what’s happened to Aleppo?

text: Sir, if I may finish my question…

text: Well, there are a quarter of a million people still living there and being slaughtered.

text: Well, Aleppo is a disaster. It’s a humanitarian nightmare. But it has fallen from the—from any standpoint. I mean, what do you need, a signed document? Take a look at Aleppo. It is so sad when you see what’s happened.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … in many cases, ISIS-aligned, and we now have them in our country, and wait until you see—this is going to be the great Trojan horse. And wait until you see what happens in the coming years. Lots of luck, Hillary. Thanks a lot for doing a great job.

text: But I just have to…

speaker: Moderator
text: Real quick.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s so ridiculous what she—she will defeat ISIS. We should have never let ISIS happen in the first place. And right now, they’re in 32 countries.

text: Mr. Trump, Secretary Clinton—no, we need to move on to our final segment, and that is the national debt, which has not been discussed until tonight.

text: Well, I say they’re wrong, because I’m going to create tremendous jobs. And we’re bringing GDP from, really, 1 percent, which is what it is now, and if she got in, it will be less than zero. text: Yeah, yeah, we’ve heard—we’ve heard this before, Hillary.

text: I started off with—my dad was a small-business man.

text: We’ve heard this before.

text: And I think it—you know, it’s a difference that affects how we see the world and what we want to do with the economy.

speaker: Donald Trump

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, no, sir, because we’re running out of time…

text: Because I did disagree with Ronald Reagan very strongly on trade. I disagreed with him. We should have been much tougher on trade even then. I’ve been waiting for years. Nobody does it right.

text: All right. The one last area I want to get into with you in this debate is the fact that the biggest driver of our debt is entitlements, which is 60 percent of all federal spending. text: That’s not going to help in the entitlements.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, it’s going to totally help you. And one thing we have to do: Repeal and replace the disaster known as Obamacare. It’s destroying our country. It’s destroying our businesses, our small business and our big businesses. We have to repeal and replace Obamacare.

speaker: Moderator
text: And, Secretary Clinton, same question, because at this point, Social Security and Medicare are going to run out, the trust funds are going to run out of money. Will you as president entertain—will you consider a grand bargain, a deal that includes both tax increases and benefit cuts to try to save both programs?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, Chris, I am on record as saying that we need to put more money into the Social Security Trust Fund. That’s part of my commitment to raise taxes on the wealthy. My Social Security payroll contribution will go up, as will Donald’s, assuming he can’t figure out how to get out of it. But what we want to do is to replenish the Social Security Trust Fund…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Such a nasty woman.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … by making sure that we have sufficient resources, and that will come from either raising the cap and/or finding other ways to get more money into it. I will not cut benefits. I want to enhance benefits for low-income workers and for women who have been disadvantaged by the current Social Security system.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Your husband disagrees with you.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … the long-term health care drivers. We’ve got to get costs down, increase value, emphasize wellness. I have a plan for doing that. And I think that we will be able to get entitlement spending under control by with more resources and smarter decisions.

speaker: Moderator
text: This is—this is the final time, probably to both of your delight, that you’re going to be on a stage together in this campaign. I would like to end it on a positive note. You had not agreed to closing statements, but it seems to me in a funny way that might make it more interesting because you haven’t prepared closing statements.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I would like to say to everyone watching tonight that I’m reaching out to all Americans—Democrats, Republicans, and independents—because we need everybody to help make our country what it should be, to grow the economy, to make it fairer, to make it work for everyone. We need your talents, your skills, your commitments, your energy, your ambition.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, thank you.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She’s raising the money from the people she wants to control. Doesn’t work that way.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thank you both. [applause]

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, thank you for being here tonight, and, Governor Pence, welcome. It is so great to be back at Longwood University in Farmville, Virginia.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, first off, thank you, Elaine, and thank you to — thank you to Norwood University for their wonderful hospitality and the Commission on Presidential Debates. It’s deeply humbling for me to be here, to be surrounded by my — my wonderful family.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine, on the campaign trail, you praised Secretary Clinton’s character, including her commitment to public service, yet 60 percent of voters don’t think she’s trustworthy. Why do so many people distrust her? Is it because they have questions about her e-mails and the Clinton Foundation?

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, let me tell you why I trust Hillary Clinton. Here’s what people should look at as they look at a public servant. Do they have a passion in their life that showed up before they were in public life? And have they held onto that passion throughout their life, regardless of whether they were in office or not, succeeding or failing?

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence, let me ask you, you have said Donald Trump is, quote, “thoughtful, compassionate, and steady.” Yet 67 percent of voters feel he is a risky choice, and 65 percent feel he does not have the right kind of temperament to be president. Why do so many Americans think Mr. Trump is simply too erratic?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, let me — let me say first and foremost that, Senator, you and Hillary Clinton would know a lot about an insult-driven campaign. It really is remarkable. At a time when literally, in the wake of Hillary Clinton’s tenure as secretary of state, where she was the architect of the Obama administration’s foreign policy, we see entire portions of the world, particularly the wider Middle East, literally spinning out of control. I mean, the situation we’re watching hour by hour in Syria today is the result of the failed foreign policy and the weak foreign policy that Hillary Clinton helped lead in this administration and create. The newly emboldened — the aggression of Russia, whether it was in Ukraine or now their heavy-handed approach…

speaker: Kaine
text: You guys love Russia. You both have said…

speaker: Pence
text: … their heavy-handed approach.

speaker: Kaine
text: You both have said — you both have said Vladimir Putin is a better leader than the president.

speaker: Pence
text: Well…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: Well, we’re going to get to Russia in just a moment. But I do want to get back to the question at…

speaker: Pence
text: But in the midst — Elaine, thank you. Thank you. Thank you, Senator, I’ll…

speaker: Kaine
text: These guys have praised Vladimir Putin as a great leader. How can that…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: Yes, and we will get to that, Senator. We do have that coming up here. But in the meantime, the questions…

speaker: Pence
text: Well, Senator, I must have hit a…[crosstalk]…I must have hit a nerve here.

speaker: Quijano
text: Why the disconnect?

speaker: Pence
text: Because at a time of great challenge in the life of this nation, where we’ve weakened America’s place in the world, stifled America’s economy, the campaign of Hillary Clinton and Tim Kaine has been an avalanche of insults.

speaker: Kaine
text: And paid few taxes and lost a billion a year.

speaker: Quijano
text: And why the disconnect with your running mate?

speaker: Pence
text: But there’s a — there’s a reason why people question the trustworthiness of Hillary Clinton. And that’s because they’re paying attention. I mean, the reality is, when she was secretary of state, Senator, come on. She had a Clinton Foundation accepting contributions from foreign governments.

speaker: Kaine
text: You are Donald Trump’s apprentice. Let me talk about this…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, I think I’m still on my time.

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, I think — isn’t this a discussion?

speaker: Quijano
text: This is our open discussion.

speaker: Kaine
text: Yeah, let’s talk about the state of…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: Well, let me interrupt — let me interrupt you and finish my sentence, if I can.

speaker: Kaine
text: Finish your sentence.

speaker: Pence
text: The Clinton Foundation accepted foreign contributions from foreign governments and foreign donors while she was secretary of state.

speaker: Kaine
text: OK, now I can weigh in. Now…

speaker: Pence
text: She had a private server…

speaker: Kaine
text: Now, I get to weigh in. Now, let me just say this…

speaker: Pence
text: … that was discovered…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: … Senator, you have an opportunity to respond.

speaker: Pence
text: … keep that pay to play process out of the reach of the public.

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor Pence — Governor Pence doesn’t think the world’s going so well and he, you know, is going to say it’s everybody’s fault.

speaker: Kaine
text: Let me tell you this. When Hillary Clinton became secretary of state, Governor Pence, do you know that Osama bin Laden was alive?

speaker: Kaine
text: Do you know that we had 175,000 troops deployed in the battlefield in Iraq and Afghanistan? Do you know that Iran was racing toward a nuclear weapon and Russia was expanding its stockpile?

speaker: Pence
text: Eliminate the Iranian nuclear weapons program?

speaker: Kaine
text: Absolutely, without firing a shot. And instead of 175,000 American troops deployed overseas, we now have 15,000.

speaker: Pence
text: Right and…

speaker: Kaine
text: These are very, very good things.

speaker: Pence
text: And Iraq has been overrun by ISIS, because Hillary Clinton failed to renegotiate…

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, if you want to put more American troops in Iraq, you can propose that.

speaker: Pence
text: Hillary Clinton — Hillary Clinton — Hillary Clinton failed to renegotiate a status of forces agreement…

speaker: Kaine
text: No, that is incorrect. That’s incorrect.

speaker: Pence
text: And so we removed — we removed all of our…

speaker: Quijano
text: Gentlemen, we’ll get to…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: … troops from Iraq, and ISIS was able to be conjured up in that vacuum.

speaker: Kaine
text: But I’d like to correct…

speaker: Pence
text: … and overrun vast areas of Iraq.

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor, President Bush said we would leave Iraq at the end of 2011. And, Elaine, Iraq didn’t want our troops to stay, and they wouldn’t give us the protection for our troops. And guess what? If a nation where our troops are serving does not want us to stay, we’re not going to stay without their protection.

speaker: Pence
text: It was a failure of the secretary of state…

speaker: Quijano
text: We need to move on to the next topic, gentlemen.

speaker: Kaine
text: If Governor Pence wants to put more troops back in Iraq, that’s…

speaker: Quijano
text: There are a lot of people wondering in this country about the economy. Let’s turn to the issue of the economy.

speaker: Quijano
text: According to the nonpartisan Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, neither of your economic plans will reduce the growing $19 trillion gross national debt. In fact, your plans would add even more to it.

speaker: Pence
text: I think the fact that — that under this past administration of which Hillary Clinton was a part, we’ve almost doubled the national debt is atrocious. I mean, I’m very proud of the fact that — I come from a state that works. The state of Indiana has balanced budgets. We cut taxes, we’ve made record investments in education and in infrastructure, and I still finish my term with $2 billion in the bank.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine?

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, on the economy, there’s a fundamental choice for the American electorate. Do you want a “you’re hired” president in Hillary Clinton or do you want a “you’re fired” president in Donald Trump? I think that’s not such a hard choice.

speaker: Quijano
text: On that point, Governor Pence, recently the New York Times released part of Mr. Trump’s 1995 tax return and reported that he could have avoided paying federal income taxes for years. Yesterday, Mr. Trump said he brilliantly used the laws to pay as little tax as legally possible. Does that seem fair to you?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, first, let me say, I appreciated the “you’re hired,” “you’re fired” thing, Senator. You use that a whole lot. And I think your running mate used a lot of pre-done lines.

speaker: Kaine
text: Fifteen million new jobs?

speaker: Pence
text: … slowest economic recovery since the Great Depression.

speaker: Kaine
text: Fifteen million new jobs?

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: There are millions more people living in poverty today than the day that Barack Obama with Hillary Clinton at his side…

speaker: Kaine
text: And the poverty level and the median income…

speaker: Pence
text: … stepped into the Oval Office.

speaker: Kaine
text: … improved dramatically between 2014 and 2015.

speaker: Pence
text: You — honestly, Senator, you can roll out the numbers and the sunny side, but I got to tell you, people in Scranton know different. People in Fort Wayne, Indiana, know different. I mean, this economy is struggling. The answer to this economy is not more taxes.

speaker: Kaine
text: But it’s not the giveaway tax relief to the folks at the top.

speaker: Pence
text: It’s not more spending…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: I am interested to hear whether he’ll defend his running mate’s not releasing taxes and not paying taxes.

speaker: Pence
text: Absolutely I will.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, with all due respect, the question was about whether it seems fair to you that Mr. Trump said he brilliantly used the laws to pay as little tax as legally possible.

speaker: Pence
text: Well, this is probably the difference between Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton and Senator Kaine. And, I mean, Hillary Clinton and Senator Kaine — God bless you for it, career public servants, that’s great — Donald Trump is a businessman, not a career politician. He actually built a business.

speaker: Kaine
text: But why won’t he release his tax returns?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, we’re answering the question about — about a business thing, is he…

speaker: Kaine
text: I do want to come back to that, but…

speaker: Pence
text: His tax returns — his tax returns showed he went through a very difficult time, but he used the tax code just the way it’s supposed to be used. And he did it brilliantly.

speaker: Kaine
text: How do you know that? You haven’t seen his tax returns.

speaker: Pence
text: He created a runway — because he’s created a business that’s worth billions of dollars today.

speaker: Kaine
text: How do you know that?

speaker: Pence
text: And with regard to paying taxes, this whole riff about not paying taxes and people saying he didn’t pay taxes for years, Donald Trump has created tens of thousands of jobs. And he’s paid payroll taxes, sales taxes, property taxes…

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, let me talk about something.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator, I’m going to give you about 30 seconds to respond, and I have question on Social Security for you.

speaker: Pence
text: The only issue on taxes — Hillary Clinton is going to raise taxes, and Donald Trump and I are going to cut them.

speaker: Kaine
text: Donald Trump started this campaign in 2014 and he said, “If I run for president, I will absolutely release my taxes.” He’s broken his first…

speaker: Pence
text: And he will.

speaker: Kaine
text: He’s broken his first promise. Second, he stood on the stage…

speaker: Pence
text: He hasn’t broken his promise. He said he’s…

speaker: Kaine
text: He stood on the stage last week and when Hillary said, you haven’t been paying taxes, he said, “That makes me smart.” So it’s smart not to pay for our military? It’s smart not to pay for veterans? It’s smart not to pay for teachers? And I guess all of us who do pay for those things, I guess we’re stupid. And the last thing I’ll say is this…

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, do you take all the deductions that you’re entitled to?

speaker: Kaine
text: The last thing — the last thing I want to ask Governor Pence is…

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor Pence had to give Donald Trump his tax returns to show he was qualified to be vice president. Donald Trump must give the American public his tax returns to show that he’s qualified to be president. And he’s breaking his promise.

speaker: Pence
text: Elaine, I have to respond to this.

speaker: Quijano
text: You get very little time, 20 seconds.

speaker: Pence
text: I’ll be — I’ll be very respectful.

speaker: Pence
text: Look, Donald Trump has filed over 100 pages of financial disclosure, which is what the law requires.

speaker: Kaine
text: But he said he would release his tax returns.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right, Gentlemen…

speaker: Pence
text: The American people can review that. And he’s going — Senator, he’s going to release his tax returns when the audit is over…

speaker: Quijano
text: … I need to ask you about Social Security…

speaker: Kaine
text: Richard Nixon released tax returns when he was under audit.

speaker: Pence
text: They’re going to raise your taxes. We’re going to cut your taxes.

speaker: Quijano
text: Gentlemen…

speaker: Kaine
text: If you can’t meet Nixon’s standard…

speaker: Quijano
text: The people at home cannot understand either one of you when you speak over each other. I would please ask you to wait until it is that the other is finished.

speaker: Kaine
text: All right. We’re having fun up here.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine, on the issue of Social Security, in 18 years, when the Social Security Trust Funds run out of money, you’ll be 76. The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget estimates your benefits could be cut by as much as $7,500 per year. What would your administration do to prevent this cut?

speaker: Kaine
text: First, we’re going to protect Social Security, which is one of the greatest programs that the American government has ever done. It happened at a time when you would work your whole life, your whole life, raising your kids, working, being a Little League coach or a Sunday school teacher, and then you would retire into poverty. And Social Security has enabled people to retire with dignity and overwhelmingly not be in poverty.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence, I’ll give you an opportunity to respond.

speaker: Pence
text: Well, thanks, Elaine. There they go again. OK…

speaker: Kaine
text: Go read — go read the book.

speaker: Pence
text: All Donald Trump — all Donald Trump and I have said about Social Security is we’re going to meet our obligations to our seniors. That’s it.

speaker: Kaine
text: Go read the book.

speaker: Pence
text: We’ve said we’re going to meet the obligations of Medicare. That’s what this campaign is really about, Senator. And I get, this is — this is the old scare tactic that they roll out…

speaker: Kaine
text: But — but you have a voting record, Governor.

speaker: Pence
text: And I get all of that. I just, look…

speaker: Pence
text: There’s a question that you asked a little bit earlier that I want to go back to.

speaker: Kaine
text: I can’t believe that you won’t defend your own voting record.

speaker: Pence
text: I have to go back to.

speaker: Pence
text: Well, look, I — you’re running with Hillary Clinton, who wants to raise taxes by $1 trillion, increase spending by $2 trillion, and you say you’re going to keep the promises of Social Security. Donald Trump and I are going to cut taxes. We’re going to — we’re going to — we’re going to…

speaker: Kaine
text: You’re not going to cut taxes. You’re going to raise taxes on the middle class.

speaker: Pence
text: … reform government programs so we can meet the obligations of Social Security and Medicare.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right. PENCE: Stay on the path that your party has us on, we’re going to be in a — in a mountain range of debt. And we’re going to face hard choices and…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: You did ask this question about debt, and the debt explosion on the Trump plan is much, much bigger than anything on the Clinton side.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right. Let me move on now…

speaker: Pence
text: Three hundred and five economists said your plan is bad for the economy.

speaker: Quijano
text: … to the issue of law enforcement and race relations. Law enforcement and race relations. After the Dallas police shooting, Police Chief David Brown said, quote, “We’re asking cops to do too much in this country. Every societal failure we put it off on the cops to solve. Not enough mental health funding, not enough drug addiction funding, schools fail, let’s give it to the cops.”

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, I think that’s a very fair comment. I think we put a lot on police shoulders. And this is something I got a lot of scar tissue and experience on.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: You know, my uncle was a cop, a career cop, on the beat in downtown Chicago. He was my hero when I was growing up. And we’d go up to visit my dad’s family in Chicago. My three brothers and I would marvel at my uncle when he would come out in his uniform, sidearm at his side.

speaker: Kaine
text: Can I — can I explain…

speaker: Pence
text: … I just think what we ought to do is we ought to stop seizing on these moments of tragedy. We ought to assure the public that we’ll have a full and complete and transparent investigation whenever there’s a loss of life because of police action. But, Senator, please, you know, enough of this seeking every opportunity to demean law enforcement broadly by making the accusation of implicit bias every time tragedy occurs.

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine — Elaine, people shouldn’t be afraid to bring up issues of bias in law enforcement. And if you’re afraid to have…

speaker: Pence
text: I’m not afraid to bring that up.

speaker: Kaine
text: And if — if you’re afraid to have the discussion, you’ll never solve it. And so here’s — here’s an example, heartbreaking. We would agree this is a heartbreaking example.

speaker: Pence
text: We need criminal justice reform.

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, we do.

speaker: Pence
text: Indiana has passed criminal justice reform.

speaker: Kaine
text: But I just want to say, those who say that we should not…

speaker: Pence
text: But that’s not what you’re talking about.

speaker: Kaine
text: … we should not be able to bring up and talk about bias in the system, we’ll never solve the problem…

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence…[crosstalk]…Governor Pence…

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, when African-American police officers involved in a police action shooting involving an African-American, why would Hillary Clinton accuse that African-American police officer of implicit bias?

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, I guess I can’t believe you are defending the position that there is no bias and it’s a topic we don’t even…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence, I have a question on that point.

speaker: Pence
text: I did not make that statement. I…

speaker: Quijano
text: Your fellow Republican, Governor Pence, Senator Tim Scott, who is African-American, recently spoke on the Senate floor. He said he was stopped seven times by law enforcement in one year.

speaker: Kaine
text: A U.S. senator.

speaker: Quijano
text: He said, “I have felt the anger, the frustration, the sadness, and the humiliation that comes with feeling like you’re being targeted for nothing more than being just yourself.” What would you say to Senator Scott about his experiences?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, I have the deepest respect for Senator Scott, and he’s a close friend. And what I would say is that we — we need to adopt criminal justice reform nationally. I — I signed criminal justice reform in the state of Indiana, Senator, and we’re very proud of it.

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, can I…

speaker: Quijano
text: So what would you say to Senator Scott, Governor?

speaker: Pence
text: Law enforcement in this country is a force for good. They are the — they truly are people that put their lives on the line every single day. But I would — I would suggest to you, what we need to do is assert a stronger leadership at the national level to support law enforcement. You just heard Senator Kaine reject stop-and-frisk. Well, I would suggest to you that the families that live in our inner cities that are besieged by crime…

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, let me — let me…

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, the question is about Senator Scott. What would — what would you tell Senator Scott?

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, if I could — if I could jump in. I’ve heard Senator Scott make that eloquent plea. And look, criminal justice is about respecting the law and being respected by the law. So there is a fundamental respect issue here.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right. I want to turn to our next segment now, immigration. Your running mates have both said that undocumented immigrants who have committed violent crimes should be deported. What would you tell the millions of undocumented immigrants who have not committed violent crimes? Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: Donald Trump’s laid out a plan to end illegal immigration once and for all in this country. We’ve been talking it to death for 20 years. Hillary Clinton and Tim Kaine want to continue the policies of open borders, amnesty, catch and release, sanctuary cities, all the things that are driving — that are driving wages down in this country, Senator, and also too often with criminal aliens in the country, it’s bringing heartbreak.

speaker: Pence
text: It’s my time, Senator.

speaker: Quijano
text: It is, in fact, the governor’s time.

speaker: Kaine
text: I apologize. It’s your two minutes. I apologize.

speaker: Pence
text: Thanks. I forgive you. He says ours is an insult-driven campaign. Did you all just hear that? Ours is an insult-driven campaign?

speaker: Pence
text: That’s small potatoes compared to Hillary Clinton…

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine?

speaker: Pence
text: …. calling half of Donald Trump’s supporters a basket of deplorables.

speaker: Kaine
text: Hillary Clinton said something on the campaign trail, and the very next day, she said, you know what, I shouldn’t have said that.

speaker: Pence
text: She said she shouldn’t have said half.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, this is Senator Kaine’s two minutes, please.

speaker: Kaine
text: Yeah, that’s right, so now we’re even.

speaker: Pence
text: Yeah. [laughter]

speaker: Kaine
text: Look for Donald Trump apologizing to John McCain for saying he wasn’t a hero…

speaker: Kaine
text: … to Donald Trump apologizing for calling women slobs, pigs, dogs, disgusting.

speaker: Pence
text: She apologized for saying “half.”

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor. It is his two minutes, please.

speaker: Kaine
text: Did Donald Trump apologize for taking after somebody in a Twitter war and making fun of her weight? Did he apologize for saying African-Americans are living in Hell? Did he apologize for saying President Obama was not even a citizen of the United States? You will look in vain to see Donald Trump ever taking responsibility for anybody and apologizing.

speaker: Pence
text: That’s nonsense. That’s nonsense.

speaker: Kaine
text: I cannot believe that Governor Pence would sit here and defend his running mate’s claim that we should create a deportation force to — so that they’ll all be gone.

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, we have a deportation force. It’s called Immigrations and Customs Enforcement. And the union for Immigrations and Customs Enforcement for the first time in their history endorsed Donald Trump to be the next president of the United States of America.

speaker: Kaine
text: So you like the 16 million deportations?

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, that’s — that’s nonsense. Look, what you just heard is they have a plan for open borders, amnesty. That’s…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: Our plan is like Ronald Reagan’s plan from 1986.

speaker: Pence
text: They call it comprehensive immigration reform — they call it comprehensive immigration reform on Capitol Hill. We all know the routine. It’s amnesty. And you heard one of the last things he mentioned was border security.

speaker: Pence
text: They always say we’re going to do this, we’re going to do that, we’ll eventually get the border…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: … border security three years ago, and Governor Pence was against it.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, Mr. Trump has said…

speaker: Pence
text: Ronald Reagan said a nation without borders is not a nation. Donald Trump is committed to restoring the borders of this nation and securing our nation, enforcing our laws.

speaker: Quijano
text: So, Governor, how would these millions of undocumented immigrants leave? Would they be forcibly removed?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, I think Donald Trump laid out a series of priorities that doesn’t ends with border security. It begins with border security. And after we secure the border, not only build a wall, but beneath the ground and in the air, we do internal enforcement.

speaker: Kaine
text: I just have to correct Governor Pence….

speaker: Pence
text: … where people can come into this country.

speaker: Kaine
text: I have to…

speaker: Pence
text: That’s the order that you should do it. Border security, removing criminal aliens, upholding with law, and then — but then, Senator, I’ll work you when you go back to the Senate, I promise you, we’ll work with you to reform the immigration system.

speaker: Kaine
text: I look forward to working together in whatever capacities we serve in. But I just want to make it very, very clear that he’s trying to fuzz up what Donald Trump has said. When Donald Trump spoke in Phoenix, he looked the audience in the eye and he said, no, we’re building a wall, and we’re deporting everybody. He said, quote, “They will all be gone.” “They will all be gone.” And this is one of these ones where you can just go to the tape on it and see what Donald Trump has said. And to add…

speaker: Pence
text: He’s talking about criminal aliens.

speaker: Kaine
text: And to add to it, and to add to it, and to add to it, we are a nation of immigrants. Mike Pence and I both are descended from immigrant families. Some things, you know, maybe weren’t said so great about the Irish when they came, but we’ve done well by absorbing immigrants, and it’s made our nation stronger.

speaker: Quijano
text: Gentleman, I’d like to shift now to the threat of terrorism. Do you think the world today is a safer or more dangerous place than it was eight years ago? Has the terrorist threat increased or decreased? Senator Kaine?

speaker: Kaine
text: The terrorist threat has decreased in some ways, because bin Laden is dead. The terrorist threat has decreased in some ways because an Iranian nuclear weapons program has been stopped. The terrorist threat to United States troops has been decreased in some ways because there’s not 175,000 in a dangerous part of the world. There’s only 15,000.

speaker: Pence

Now exactly what action, you would have to determine what your intelligence was, how certain you were of that intelligence, but you would have to take action.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right. I’d like to turn to our next segment now. And in this, I’d like to focus on social issues. You have both been open about the role that faith has played in your lives. Can you discuss in detail a time when you struggled to balance your personal faith and a public policy position? Senator Kaine?

speaker: Kaine
text: Yeah, that’s an easy one for me, Elaine. It’s an easy one. I’m really fortunate. I grew up in a wonderful household with great Irish Catholic parents. My mom and dad are sitting right here. I was educated by Jesuits at Rockhurst High School in Kansas City. My 40th reunion is in 10 days.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, it’s a wonderful question. And my Christian faith is at the very heart of who I am. I was also raised in a wonderful family of faith. It was a church on Sunday morning and grace before dinner.

speaker: Kaine
text: That’s shared.

speaker: Pence
text: But for me, I would tell you that for me the sanctity of life proceeds out of the belief that — that ancient principle that — where God says before you were formed in the womb, I knew you, and so for my first time in public life, I sought to stand with great compassion for the sanctity of life.

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, this is a fundamental question, a fundamental question. Hillary and I are both people out of religious backgrounds, from Methodist church experience, which was really formative for her as a public servant.

speaker: Pence
text: No, it’s really not. Donald Trump and I would never support legislation that punished women who made the heartbreaking choice to end a pregnancy.

speaker: Kaine
text: Then why did Donald Trump say that?

speaker: Pence
text: We just never would.

speaker: Kaine
text: Why did he say that?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, look, it’s — look, he’s not a polished politician like you and Hillary Clinton. And so…

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, I would admit that’s not a polished…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: You know, things don’t always come out exactly the way he means them.

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, can I say…

speaker: Pence
text: But I’m telling you what the policy of our administration would be.

speaker: Kaine
text: Great line from the — great line from the gospel of Matthew. From the fullness of the heart, the mouth speaks.

speaker: Kaine
text: When Donald Trump says women should be punished or Mexicans are rapists and criminals…

speaker: Pence
text: I’m telling you…

speaker: Kaine
text: … or John McCain is not a hero, he is showing you who he is.

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, you’ve whipped out that Mexican thing again. He — look…

speaker: Kaine
text: Can you defend it?

speaker: Pence
text: There are criminal aliens in this country, Tim, who have come into this country illegally who are perpetrating violence and taking American lives.

speaker: Kaine
text: You want to — you want to use a big broad brush against Mexicans on that?

speaker: Pence
text: He also said and many of them are good people. You keep leaving that out of your quote. And if you want me to go there, I’ll go there.

speaker: Kaine
text: This is important —

speaker: Pence
text: … bring the — let’s welcome the children into our world. There are so many families around the country who can’t have children. We could improve adoption…

speaker: Kaine
text: But, Governor…

speaker: Pence
text: … so that families that can’t have children can adopt more readily those children from crisis pregnancies.

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor, why don’t you trust women to make this choice for themselves? We can encourage people to support life. Of course we can. But why don’t you trust women? Why doesn’t Donald Trump trust women to make this choice for themselves?

speaker: Pence
text: Because there are…

speaker: Kaine
text: … but on fundamental issues of morality, we should let women make their own decisions.

speaker: Pence
text: Because there is — a society can be judged by how it deals with its most vulnerable, the aged, the infirm, the disabled, and the unborn. I believe it with all my heart. And I couldn’t be more proud to be standing with a pro-life candidate in Donald Trump.

speaker: Quijano
text: I do have one final question for you both tonight. It has been a divisive campaign. Senator Kaine, if your ticket wins, what specifically are you going to do to unify the country and reassure the people who voted against you?

speaker: Kaine
text: That’s a really important one. That may be the $64,000 question, because it has been a divisive campaign. And again, Hillary is running a campaign about stronger together, and Donald Trump — and this is — this is not directed at this man, except to the extent that he can’t defend Donald Trump — Donald Trump has run a campaign that’s been about one insult after the next.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, how will you unify the country if you win?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, thank you, Elaine, and thanks for a great discussion…

speaker: Kaine
text: Absolutely.

speaker: Pence
text: … tonight. Thank you, Senator.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right, gentlemen, thank you so much.

speaker: Cooper
text: And I’m Anderson Cooper from CNN. We want to welcome you to Washington University in St. Louis for the second presidential debate between Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump, sponsored by the Commission on Presidential Debates. Tonight’s debate is a town hall format, which gives voters a chance to directly ask the candidates questions. Martha and I will ask follow-up questions but the night really belongs to the people in this room, and to people across the country who have submitted questions online.

speaker: Raddatz
text: The people you see on this stage were chosen by the Gallup Organization. They are all from the St. Louis area and told Gallup they haven’t committed to a candidate. Each of them came here with questions they wanted to ask, and we saw those questions for the first time this morning. Anderson and I and our team from ABC and CNN are the only ones who have seen them. Both candidates will have two minutes to answer each audience and online question. We hope to get to as many questions as we can, so we’ve asked the audience here not to slow things down with any applause. Except for now.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Ladies and gentlemen the Republican nominee for president, Donald J. Trump, and the Democratic nominee for president, Hillary Clinton. [applause]

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you very much for being here. We’re going to begin with a question from one of the members in our town hall. Each of you will have two minutes to respond to this question. Secretary Clinton, you won the coin toss, so you’ll go first. Our first question comes from Patrice Brock. Patrice?

speaker: Question
text: Thank you, and good evening. The last presidential debate could have been rated as MA, mature audiences, per TV parental guidelines. Knowing that educators assign viewing the presidential debates as students’ homework, do you feel you’re modeling appropriate and positive behavior for today’s youth?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, thank you. Are you a teacher? Yes, I think that that’s a very good question, because I’ve heard from lots of teachers and parents about some of their concerns about some of the things that are being said and done in this campaign.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton, thank you. Mr. Trump, you have two minutes.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, I actually agree with that. I agree with everything she said. I began this campaign because I was so tired of seeing such foolish things happen to our country. This is a great country. This is a great land. I’ve gotten to know the people of the country over the last year-and-a-half that I’ve been doing this as a politician. I cannot believe I’m saying that about myself, but I guess I have been a politician.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, Mr. Trump. The question from Patrice was about are you both modeling positive and appropriate behavior for today’s youth? We received a lot of questions online, Mr. Trump, about the tape that was released on Friday, as you can imagine. You called what you said locker room banter. You described kissing women without consent, grabbing their genitals. That is sexual assault. You bragged that you have sexually assaulted women. Do you understand that?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, I didn’t say that at all. I don’t think you understood what was—this was locker room talk. I’m not proud of it. I apologize to my family. I apologize to the American people. Certainly, I’m not proud of it. But this is locker room talk.

speaker: Cooper
text: So, Mr. Trump…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And we should get on to much more important things and much bigger things.

speaker: Cooper
text: Just for the record, though, are you saying that what you said on that bus 11 years ago that you did not actually kiss women without consent or grope women without consent?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I have great respect for women. Nobody has more respect for women than I do.

speaker: Cooper
text: So, for the record, you’re saying you never did that?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I’ve said things that, frankly, you hear these things I said. And I was embarrassed by it. But I have tremendous respect for women.

speaker: Cooper
text: Have you ever done those things?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And women have respect for me. And I will tell you: No, I have not. And I will tell you that I’m going to make our country safe. We’re going to have borders in our country, which we don’t have now. People are pouring into our country, and they’re coming in from the Middle East and other places.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, Mr. Trump.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Right now, other nations are taking our jobs and they’re taking our wealth.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, Mr. Trump.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And that’s what I want to talk about.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton, do you want to respond?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, like everyone else, I’ve spent a lot of time thinking over the last 48 hours about what we heard and saw. You know, with prior Republican nominees for president, I disagreed with them on politics, policies, principles, but I never questioned their fitness to serve.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And we want to get to some questions from online…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Am I allowed to respond to that? I assume I am.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Yes, you can respond to that.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s just words, folks. It’s just words. Those words, I’ve been hearing them for many years. I heard them when they were running for the Senate in New York, where Hillary was going to bring back jobs to upstate New York and she failed.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Trump, Mr. Trump—I want to get to audience questions and online questions.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: So, she’s allowed to do that, but I’m not allowed to respond?

speaker: Raddatz
text: You’re going to have—you’re going to get to respond right now.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Sounds fair.

speaker: Raddatz
text: This tape is generating intense interest. In just 48 hours, it’s become the single most talked about story of the entire 2016 election on Facebook, with millions and millions of people discussing it on the social network. As we said a moment ago, we do want to bring in questions from voters around country via social media, and our first stays on this topic. Jeff from Ohio asks on Facebook, “Trump says the campaign has changed him. When did that happen?” So, Mr. Trump, let me add to that. When you walked off that bus at age 59, were you a different man or did that behavior continue until just recently? And you have two minutes for this.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It was locker room talk, as I told you. That was locker room talk. I’m not proud of it. I am a person who has great respect for people, for my family, for the people of this country. And certainly, I’m not proud of it. But that was something that happened.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Can we please hold the applause? Secretary Clinton, you have two minutes.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, first, let me start by saying that so much of what he’s just said is not right, but he gets to run his campaign any way he chooses. He gets to decide what he wants to talk about. Instead of answering people’s questions, talking about our agenda, laying out the plans that we have that we think can make a better life and a better country, that’s his choice.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, you owe the president an apology, because as you know very well, your campaign, Sidney Blumenthal—he’s another real winner that you have—and he’s the one that got this started, along with your campaign manager, and they were on television just two weeks ago, she was, saying exactly that. So you really owe him an apology. You’re the one that sent the pictures around your campaign, sent the pictures around with President Obama in a certain garb. That was long before I was ever involved, so you actually owe an apology.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Secretary Clinton, I want to follow up on that.

speaker: Raddatz
text: I’m going to let you talk about e-mails.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … because everything he just said is absolutely false, but I’m not surprised.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Oh, really?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: In the first debate…[laughter]

speaker: Raddatz
text: And really, the audience needs to calm down here.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … I told people that it would be impossible to be fact-checking Donald all the time. I’d never get to talk about anything I want to do and how we’re going to really make lives better for people.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Because you’d be in jail. [applause]

speaker: Raddatz
text: Secretary Clinton…

speaker: Cooper
text: We want to remind the audience to please not talk out loud. Please do not applaud. You’re just wasting time.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And, Secretary Clinton, I do want to follow up on e- mails. You’ve said your handing of your e-mails was a mistake. You disagreed with FBI Director James Comey, calling your handling of classified information, quote, “extremely careless.” The FBI said that there were 110 classified e-mails that were exchanged, eight of which were top secret, and that it was possible hostile actors did gain access to those e-mails. You don’t call that extremely careless?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, Martha, first, let me say—and I’ve said before, but I’ll repeat it, because I want everyone to hear it—that was a mistake, and I take responsibility for using a personal e-mail account. Obviously, if I were to do it over again, I would not. I’m not making any excuses. It was a mistake. And I am very sorry about that.

speaker: Raddatz
text: OK, we’re going to move on.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And yet she didn’t know the word—the letter C on a document. Right? She didn’t even know what that word—what that letter meant.

speaker: Cooper
text: We have to move on.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You did that. Wait a minute. One second.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton, you can respond, and then we’ve got to move on.

speaker: Raddatz
text: We want to give the audience a chance.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: If you did that in the private sector, you’d be put in jail, let alone after getting a subpoena from the United States Congress.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton, you can respond. Then we have to move on to an audience question.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Look, it’s just not true. And so please, go to…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Oh, you didn’t delete them?

speaker: Cooper
text: Allow her to respond, please.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: It was personal e-mails, not official.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Oh, 33,000? Yeah.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Not—well, we turned over 35,000, so…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Oh, yeah. What about the other 15,000?

speaker: Cooper
text: Please allow her to respond. She didn’t talk while you talked.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Yes, that’s true, I didn’t.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Because you have nothing to say.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: I didn’t in the first debate, and I’m going to try not to in this debate, because I’d like to get to the questions that the people have brought here tonight to talk to us about.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And get off this question.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: OK, Donald. I know you’re into big diversion tonight, anything to avoid talking about your campaign and the way it’s exploding and the way Republicans are leaving you. But let’s at least focus…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Let’s see what happens…[crosstalk]

speaker: Cooper
text: Allow her to respond.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … on some of the issues that people care about tonight. Let’s get to their questions.

speaker: Cooper
text: We have a question here from Ken Karpowicz. He has a question about health care. Ken?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I’d like to know, Anderson, why aren’t you bringing up the e-mails? I’d like to know. Why aren’t you bringing…

speaker: Cooper
text: We brought up the e-mails.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, it hasn’t. It hasn’t. And it hasn’t been finished at all.

speaker: Cooper
text: Ken Karpowicz has a question.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s nice to—one on three.

speaker: Question
text: Thank you. Affordable Care Act, known as Obamacare, it is not affordable. Premiums have gone up. Deductibles have gone up. Copays have gone up. Prescriptions have gone up. And the coverage has gone down. What will you do to bring the cost down and make coverage better?

speaker: Cooper
text: That first one goes to Secretary Clinton, because you started out the last one to the audience.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: If he wants to start, he can start. No, go ahead, Donald.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, I’m a gentleman, Hillary. Go ahead. [laughter]

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I think Donald was about to say he’s going to solve it by repealing it and getting rid of the Affordable Care Act. And I’m going to fix it, because I agree with you. Premiums have gotten too high. Copays, deductibles, prescription drug costs, and I’ve laid out a series of actions that we can take to try to get those costs down.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton, your time is up.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: So I want us to get to 100 percent, but get costs down and keep quality up.

speaker: Cooper
text: Mr. Trump, you have two minutes.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It is such a great question and it’s maybe the question I get almost more than anything else, outside of defense. Obamacare is a disaster. You know it. We all know it. It’s going up at numbers that nobody’s ever seen worldwide. Nobody’s ever seen numbers like this for health care.

speaker: Cooper
text: Mr. Trump, your time…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It is a disastrous plan, and it has to be repealed and replaced.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton, let me follow up with you. Your husband called Obamacare, quote, “the craziest thing in the world,” saying that small-business owners are getting killed as premiums double, coverage is cut in half. Was he mistaken or was the mistake simply telling the truth?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: No, I mean, he clarified what he meant. And it’s very clear. Look, we are in a situation in our country where if we were to start all over again, we might come up with a different system. But we have an employer-based system. That’s where the vast majority of people get their health care.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … get to do pretty much whatever they want, including saying, look, I’m sorry, you’ve got diabetes, you had cancer, your child has asthma…

speaker: Cooper
text: Your time is up.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … you may not be able to have insurance because you can’t afford it. So let’s fix what’s broken about it, but let’s not throw it away and give it all back to the insurance companies and the drug companies. That’s not going to work.

speaker: Cooper
text: Mr. Trump, let me follow up on this.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, I just want—just one thing. First of all, Hillary, everything’s broken about it. Everything. Number two, Bernie Sanders said that Hillary Clinton has very bad judgment. This is a perfect example of it, trying to save Obamacare, which is a disaster.

speaker: Cooper
text: You’ve said you want to end Obamacare…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: By the way…

speaker: Cooper
text: You’ve said you want to end Obamacare. You’ve also said you want to make coverage accessible for people with pre-existing conditions. How do you force insurance companies to do that if you’re no longer mandating that every American get insurance?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We’re going to be able to. You’re going to have plans…

speaker: Cooper
text: What does that mean?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, I’ll tell you what it means. You’re going to have plans that are so good, because we’re going to have so much competition in the insurance industry. Once we break out—once we break out the lines and allow the competition to come…

speaker: Cooper
text: Are you going—are you going to have a mandate that Americans have to have health insurance?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: President Obama—Anderson, excuse me. President Obama, by keeping those lines, the boundary lines around each state, it was almost gone until just very toward the end of the passage of Obamacare, which, by the way, was a fraud. You know that, because Jonathan Gruber, the architect of Obamacare, was said—he said it was a great lie, it was a big lie. President Obama said you keep your doctor, you keep your plan. The whole thing was a fraud, and it doesn’t work.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, Mr. Trump.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … so that we will be able to take care of people without the necessary funds to take care of themselves.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, Mr. Trump.

speaker: Raddatz
text: We now go to Gorbah Hamed with a question for both candidates.

speaker: Question
text: Hi. There are 3.3 million Muslims in the United States, and I’m one of them. You’ve mentioned working with Muslim nations, but with Islamophobia on the rise, how will you help people like me deal with the consequences of being labeled as a threat to the country after the election is over?

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Trump, you’re first.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, you’re right about Islamophobia, and that’s a shame. But one thing we have to do is we have to make sure that—because there is a problem. I mean, whether we like it or not, and we could be very politically correct, but whether we like it or not, there is a problem. And we have to be sure that Muslims come in and report when they see something going on. When they see hatred going on, they have to report it.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Secretary Clinton?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, thank you for asking your question. And I’ve heard this question from a lot of Muslim-Americans across our country, because, unfortunately, there’s been a lot of very divisive, dark things said about Muslims. And even someone like Captain Khan, the young man who sacrificed himself defending our country in the United States Army, has been subject to attack by Donald.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Thank you, Secretary Clinton.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: First of all, Captain Khan is an American hero, and if I were president at that time, he would be alive today, because unlike her, who voted for the war without knowing what she was doing, I would not have had our people in Iraq. Iraq was a disaster. So he would have been alive today.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And why did it morph into that? No, did you—no, answer the question. Do you still believe…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Why don’t you interrupt her? You interrupt me all the time.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Why don’t you interrupt her?

speaker: Raddatz
text: Would you please explain whether or not the Muslim ban still stands?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s called extreme vetting. We are going to areas like Syria where they’re coming in by the tens of thousands because of Barack Obama. And Hillary Clinton wants to allow a 550 percent increase over Obama. People are coming into our country like we have no idea who they are, where they are from, what their feelings about our country is, and she wants 550 percent more. This is going to be the great Trojan horse of all time.

speaker: Raddatz
text: And, Secretary Clinton, let me ask you about that, because you have asked for an increase from 10,000 to 65,000 Syrian refugees. We know you want tougher vetting. That’s not a perfect system. So why take the risk of having those refugees come into the country?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, first of all, I will not let anyone into our country that I think poses a risk to us. But there are a lot of refugees, women and children—think of that picture we all saw of that 4-year-old boy with the blood on his forehead because he’d been bombed by the Russian and Syrian air forces.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: That’s not been debunked.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: So, please…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: That has not been debunked.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … go to HillaryClinton.com and you can see it.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I was against—I was against the war in Iraq. Has not been debunked. And you voted for it. And you shouldn’t have. Well, I just want to say…

speaker: Raddatz
text: There’s been lots of fact-checking on that. I’d like to move on to an online question…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Excuse me. She just went about 25 seconds over her time.

speaker: Raddatz
text: She did not.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Could I just respond to this, please?

speaker: Raddatz
text: Very quickly, please.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Hillary Clinton, in terms of having people come into our country, we have many criminal illegal aliens. When we want to send them back to their country, their country says we don’t want them. In some cases, they’re murderers, drug lords, drug problems. And they don’t want them.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Thank you, Mr. Trump. I want to move on. This next question comes from the public through the Bipartisan Open Debate Coalition’s online forum, where Americans submitted questions that generated millions of votes. This question involves WikiLeaks release of purported excerpts of Secretary Clinton’s paid speeches, which she has refused to release, and one line in particular, in which you, Secretary Clinton, purportedly say you need both a public and private position on certain issues. So, Tu, from Virginia asks, is it OK for politicians to be two-faced? Is it acceptable for a politician to have a private stance on issues? Secretary Clinton, your two minutes.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, right. As I recall, that was something I said about Abraham Lincoln after having seen the wonderful Steven Spielberg movie called “Lincoln.” It was a master class watching President Lincoln get the Congress to approve the 13th Amendment. It was principled, and it was strategic.

speaker: Raddatz
text: We’re going to get to that later. Secretary Clinton, you’re out of time.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … with the Russians and other foreign powers.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Trump?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, I think I should respond, because—so ridiculous. Look, now she’s blaming—she got caught in a total lie. Her papers went out to all her friends at the banks, Goldman Sachs and everybody else, and she said things—WikiLeaks that just came out. And she lied. Now she’s blaming the lie on the late, great Abraham Lincoln. That’s one that I haven’t…[laughter]

speaker: Raddatz
text: Thank you, Mr. Trump.

speaker: Cooper
text: We want to turn, actually, to the topic of taxes. We have a question from Spencer Maass. Spencer?

speaker: Question
text: Good evening. My question is, what specific tax provisions will you change to ensure the wealthiest Americans pay their fair share in taxes?

speaker: Cooper
text: Mr. Trump, you have two minutes.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, one thing I’d do is get rid of carried interest. One of the greatest provisions for people like me, to be honest with you, I give up a lot when I run, because I knock out the tax code. And she could have done this years ago, by the way. She’s a United States—she was a United States senator.

speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary Clinton, you have two minutes. The question was, what specific tax provisions will you change to ensure the wealthiest Americans pay their fair share of taxes?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, everything you’ve heard just now from Donald is not true. I’m sorry I have to keep saying this, but he lives in an alternative reality. And it is sort of amusing to hear somebody who hasn’t paid federal income taxes in maybe 20 years talking about what he’s going to do.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, Secretary.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And we’re going to make sure that nobody, no corporation, and no individual can get away without paying his fair share to support our country.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you. I want to give you—Mr. Trump, I want to give you the chance to respond. I just wanted to tell our viewers what she’s referring to. In the last month, taxes were the number-one issue on Facebook for the first time in the campaign. The New York Times published three pages of your 1995 tax returns. They show you claimed a $916 million loss, which means you could have avoided paying personal federal income taxes for years. You’ve said you pay state taxes, employee taxes, real estate taxes, property taxes. You have not answered, though, a simple question. Did you use that $916 million loss to avoid paying personal federal income taxes for years?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Of course I do. Of course I do. And so do all of her donors, or most of her donors. I know many of her donors. Her donors took massive tax write-offs.

speaker: Cooper
text: So have you paid personal federal income tax?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: A lot of my—excuse me, Anderson—a lot of my write- off was depreciation and other things that Hillary as a senator allowed. And she’ll always allow it, because the people that give her all this money, they want it. That’s why.

speaker: Cooper
text: So can you—can you say how many years you have avoided paying personal federal income taxes?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, but I pay tax, and I pay federal tax, too. But I have a write-off, a lot of it’s depreciation, which is a wonderful charge. I love depreciation. You know, she’s given it to us.

speaker: Cooper
text: In the past…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And, again, Bernie Sanders, it’s really bad judgment. She has made bad judgment not only on taxes. She’s made bad judgments on Libya, on Syria, on Iraq. speaker: Cooper
text: Secretary—I want you to be able to respond, Secretary Clinton.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, here we go again. I’ve been in favor of getting rid of carried interest for years, starting when I was a senator from New York. But that’s not the point here.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Why didn’t you do it? Why didn’t you do it?

speaker: Cooper
text: Allow her to respond.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Because I was a senator with a Republican president.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Oh, really?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: I will be the president and we will get it done. That’s exactly right.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You could have done it, if you were an effective—if you were an effective senator, you could have done it. If you were an effective senator, you could have done it. But you were not an effective senator.

speaker: Cooper
text: Please allow her to respond. She didn’t interrupt you.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: You know, under our Constitution, presidents have something called veto power. Look, he has now said repeatedly, “30 years this and 30 years that.” So let me talk about my 30 years in public service. I’m very glad to do so.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, secretary.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And I’ve proven that I can, and for 30 years, I’ve produced results for people.

speaker: Cooper
text: Thank you, secretary.

speaker: Raddatz
text: We’re going to move on to Syria. Both of you have mentioned that.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She said a lot of things that were false. I mean, I think we should be allowed to maybe…

speaker: Raddatz
text: No, we can—no, Mr. Trump, we’re going to go on. This is about the audience.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Excuse me. Because she has been a disaster as a senator. A disaster.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Trump, we’re going to move on. The heart-breaking video of a 5-year-old Syrian boy named Omran sitting in an ambulance after being pulled from the rubble after an air strike in Aleppo focused the world’s attention on the horrors of the war in Syria, with 136 million views on Facebook alone.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, the situation in Syria is catastrophic. And every day that goes by, we see the results of the regime by Assad in partnership with the Iranians on the ground, the Russians in the air, bombarding places, in particular Aleppo, where there are hundreds of thousands of people, probably about 250,000 still left. speaker: Raddatz
text: Thank you, Secretary Clinton. Mr. Trump?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: First of all, she was there as secretary of state with the so-called line in the sand, which…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: No, I wasn’t. I was gone. I hate to interrupt you, but at some point…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: OK. But you were in contact—excuse me. You were…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: At some point, we need to do some fact-checking here.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You were in total contact with the White House, and perhaps, sadly, Obama probably still listened to you. I don’t think he would be listening to you very much anymore.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Trump, Mr. Trump, your two minutes is up.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And one thing I have to say.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Your two minutes is up.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I don’t like Assad at all, but Assad is killing ISIS. Russia is killing ISIS. And Iran is killing ISIS. And those three have now lined up because of our weak foreign policy.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Mr. Trump, let me repeat the question. If you were president…[laughter]…what would you do about Syria and the humanitarian crisis in Aleppo? speaker: Donald Trump
text: OK. He and I haven’t spoken, and I disagree. I disagree.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You disagree with your running mate?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think you have to knock out ISIS. Right now, Syria is fighting ISIS. We have people that want to fight both at the same time. But Syria is no longer Syria. speaker: Raddatz
text: What do you think will happen if Aleppo falls?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think Aleppo is a disaster, humanitarian-wise.

speaker: Raddatz
text: What do you think will happen if it falls?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think that it basically has fallen. OK? It basically has fallen. Let me tell you something. You take a look at Mosul. text: There are sometimes reasons the military does that. Psychological warfare.

text: I can’t think of any. I can’t think of any. And I’m pretty good at it.

text: It might be to help get civilians out.

text: And we have General Flynn. And we have—look, I have 200 generals and admirals who endorsed me. I have 21 Congressional Medal of Honor recipients who endorsed me. We talk about it all the time. text: Tell me what your strategy is.

text: … for weeks—I’ve been reading now for weeks about Mosul, that it’s the harbor of where—you know, between Raqqa and Mosul, this is where they think the ISIS leaders are. text: But what would you do differently than President Obama is doing?

text: Well, Martha, I hope that by the time I—if I’m fortunate…

speaker: Donald Trump

text: I hope by the time I am president that we will have pushed ISIS out of Iraq. I do think that there is a good chance that we can take Mosul. And, you know, Donald says he knows more about ISIS than the generals. No, he doesn’t.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Thank you very much. We’re going to move on…

text: You know what’s funny? She went over a minute over, and you don’t stop her. When I go one second over, it’s like a big deal.

speaker: Raddatz
text: You had many answers.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s really—it’s really very interesting.

text: Thank you.

text: Because we talked about what we wanted to do. We might have had some differences, and we had a lot of debates…

text: Thank you, Secretary.

text: … but we believed that we could make the country better. And I was proud of that.

text: I want to give you a minute to respond.

text: She said some of them are irredeemable.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She’s got tremendous—she’s got tremendous hatred. And this country cannot take another four years of Barack Obama, and that’s what you’re getting with her.

text: No, there wasn’t check out a sex tape. It was just take a look at the person that she built up to be this wonderful Girl Scout who was no Girl Scout.

text: You mentioned sex tape.

text: The question is, is that the discipline of a good leader?

text: Secretary Clinton, does Mr. Trump have the discipline to be a good leader?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I’m shocked to hear that. [laughter]

text: Well, it’s not only my opinion. It’s the opinion of many others, national security experts, Republicans, former Republican members of Congress. text: We have to move along.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Nine million people lost their jobs.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Secretary Clinton, we have to…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Five million homes were lost.

speaker: Raddatz
text: Secretary Clinton, we’re moving on.

text: And $13 trillion in family wealth was wiped out. We are back on the right track. He would send us back into recession with his tax plans that benefit the wealthiest of Americans.

speaker: Donald Trump

text: We begin with your two minutes, Secretary Clinton.

text: Thank you. Well, you’re right. This is one of the most important issues in this election. text: Thank you, Secretary Clinton. Thank you. You’re out of time. Mr. Trump?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well…[crosstalk]

text: Thank you very much. We’re going to get on to one more question.

text: The question was about the Supreme Court. And I just want to quickly say, I respect the Second Amendment. But I believe there should be comprehensive background checks, and we should close the gun show loophole, and close the online loophole.

text: Thank you.

text: We have—we have one more question, Mrs. Clinton.

text: We have to save as many lives as we possibly can.

text: It’s an absolute disgrace.

text: But the price of coal is down worldwide. So we have to look at this comprehensively.

text: Your time is up.

text: And that’s exactly what I have proposed. I hope you will go to HillaryClinton.com and look at my entire policy.

text: Time is up. We have time for one more…

text: One more audience question.

text: Thanks to both of you.

text: We want to thank both the candidates. We want to thank the university here. This concludes the town hall meeting. Our thanks to the candidates, the commission, Washington University, and to everybody who watched.

text: Secretary Clinton, would you like to respond?

text: Well, I think that trade is an important issue. Of course, we are 5 percent of the world’s population; we have to trade with the other 95 percent. And we need to have smart, fair trade deals.

text: Let me follow up with Mr. Trump, if I can. You’ve talked about creating 25 million jobs, and you’ve promised to bring back millions of jobs for Americans.
